ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the right-angled triangle $ABC$, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, $AB=AC$, perpendicular lines $BD$ and $CE$ are drawn from points $B$ and $C$ respectively, through point $A$, with the feet of the perpendiculars being $D$ and $E$. If $BD=4\,\text{cm}$ and $CE=3\,\text{cm}$, what is the length of $DE$ in centimeters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $BD \perp AD$ and $CE \perp AD$,\\
it follows that $\angle D = \angle E = 90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle DAB + \angle ABD = 90^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle DAB + \angle CAE = 90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle ABD = \angle CAE$,\\
Since $AB = AC$,\\
it follows that $\triangle DAB \cong \triangle ECA$ (AAS),\\
hence $BD = AE = 4\,\text{cm}, AD = CE = 3\,\text{cm}$,\\
therefore $DE = AE + AD = \boxed{7\,\text{cm}}$.

it follows that $\triangle DAB \cong \triangle ECA$ (AAS),\\
hence $BD = AE = 4\,\text{cm}, AD = CE = 3\,\text{cm}$,\\
therefore $DE = AE + AD = \boxed{7\,\text{cm}}$
